_source: Started as a transcription (not a capture) from two community Linux
projects that speak to Pulsar's Nordic wireless dongle:
packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux (drivers/nordic.py, an address-mapped
memory protocol for VID 0x3554) and andrewrabert/python-pulsar-mouse-tool,
its credited source. That gave the packet shape (17 bytes, opcode +
address + length, sum8_minus_55 checksum) but not this exact model's IDs.
Confirmed since, statically, by running tools/analyze-driver.py against
the real Pulsar Fusion Windows installer (innoextract'd, then pointed at
'Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe' and the Cfg.ini it ships) -- no
hardware capture, but real vendor source, not a secondhand description:
- Cfg.ini's [OPT] section: VID=25A7,3554  PID=fa7b,f507  PID2=fa7c,f508,f509
-- matches the 3554:f507/f509 this project already found live via
`hskctl probe` on real hardware, and adds a second vendor id (25a7,
presumably an older USB bridge chip revision, same pattern as
G-Wolves shipping several PIDs across hardware revisions) this
project has no hardware to confirm.
- Cfg.ini's [DEV_13] is this exact model: Name=X2H Mini Wireless,
CID=0x06 (shared by every wireless model in the file -- DEV_1 through
DEV_21 are all CID=0x06, meaning the app treats them as one protocol
family and tells them apart by a model id, MID=0x0D for this one),
Sensor=0x3395 (PixArt PAW3395), DPI=400,800,1600,3200 (four stages
out of the box -- NOT seven like the G-Wolves profile), Debounce=3.
This is capability/default metadata the app's UI uses, not wire-
protocol byte offsets -- it doesn't tell us where MID or the DPI
stages live in a packet, only that they exist and what a fresh X2H
mini ships with.
- The app itself ('Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe') is native C++/MFC,
not .NET or Electron -- confirmed importing HidD_SetFeature,
HidD_GetHidGuid, HidD_GetPreparsedData, HidP_GetCaps, so the transport
really is HID Feature reports, matching this profile's `transport.kind`.
But native code embeds packet bytes as immediate values in machine
code, not as a labelled blob the way .NET's FieldRVA let this same
script pull G-Wolves' HTS_*_CMD tables out directly -- so the actual
opcode/address bytes below are still the pre-existing transcription,
not decoded from this binary. Getting those needs either real
disassembly of this exe, or a live USB capture while it runs.
Every field below is marked _needsVerification, which hskctl already
treats as a hard stop on writing (see Profile.field_writable) --
exactly the gate `dpiStageCount` and the sleep timer relied on in the
G-Wolves profile before they were confirmed on hardware. Reads are
harmless even if a byte offset here is wrong: HIDIOCGFEATURE cannot
damage the device, it can only come back with a number that is
obviously not a battery percentage. Writes are where a wrong offset
gets expensive, so none are enabled here.
DPI stage values and LED colour are deliberately not mapped: the source
describes them as 4-byte records on the device with their own per-record
checksum (0x55 - value), which this engine's single packet-level
checksum has no hook for. That needs a small protocol.py addition
(a record-level checksum encoding) before it can be done honestly --
see the note on 'dpi_record_nordic' below. Until then this profile
covers battery, firmware version, polling rate, DPI stage count/index,
lift-off distance, debounce, motion sync, angle snap, ripple control,
turbo mode and the sleep timer.
status: partial means hskctl will talk to the device once the PID
matches, but every reading needs sanity-checking against the Pulsar
Fusion app on Windows before anyone trusts it -- and every write stays
refused until _needsVerification is removed field by field.

match._comment: vendorIds/productIds now match Cfg.ini's own [OPT] block from the real Pulsar Fusion installer (VID=25A7,3554  PID=fa7b,f507  PID2=fa7c,f508,f509) as well as what `hskctl probe` found live on real hardware: the cabled mouse enumerates as 3554:f507 (config endpoint on interface 11, vendor usage page 0xff04, feature report id 6 -- the wired probe's top candidate, score 125, fully identified). The RF receiver is a SEPARATE USB device, 3554:f509 ('Pulsar 4K Wireless Receiver') -- its config-endpoint interface has not been captured yet (the probe run so far only showed generic-usage-page interfaces, none of them identified). 25a7:fa7b/fa7c are Cfg.ini's alternate ids (presumably an older USB bridge chip revision) with no hardware here to confirm them against. Do NOT add 0x3710:0x1403 (X2H Wired Medium) to this profile: that model speaks a different, 64-byte, register-addressed protocol (the one x2a.py/x2h.py implement), not the 17-byte memory-mapped one this file describes -- it needs its own profile.

transport._comment: 17-byte packet length is still an unconfirmed guess -- pending `hskctl doctor --json` on the real device to see the actual reply size. reportId IS confirmed, though: hskctl probe found the cabled mouse's config endpoint (3554:f507, interface 11) reporting feature report id 6, not the unnumbered id 0 originally guessed here -- byte 0 of every packet template below was fixed to match. Whether the host writes these as HID Feature reports (like the G-Wolves profile) or Output reports over an interrupt endpoint is still unconfirmed by either source project; 'feature' matches what the probe found (a feature report id existing at all), so it is now a better-than-guess default rather than an arbitrary one.

commands._comment: Two shapes here. 'battery'/'version' are their own opcodes (byte 1) with data from byte 2, matching the G-Wolves style. Everything else rides the dongle's memory-mapped get/set (opcode 0x08 read / 0x07 write, at a fixed address baked into each command's template since every hskctl field is its own fixed address, not a runtime parameter) -- byte 3:4 address (endianness unconfirmed, written big-endian here), byte 5 length, value from byte 6.

battery._note: [6]=percent, [7]=power/charging, [8:10]=millivolts per the nordic.py summary. Only percent and charging are mapped here; battery_mv would need a u16 field of its own once confirmed.

pollingRate._note: address 0x00. The raw<->Hz mapping (POLL_VAL_TO_HZ in the source) was not itself transcribed, so no `values` map is given -- see the field below.

sleep._note: address 0xb7, described as 'units of 10s'; encoded below with scale:10 so the field itself still speaks seconds.

batteryPercent._needsVerification: byte offset transcribed from a summary of nordic.py, not read from source or hardware

firmwareVersion._needsVerification: offset transcribed, not confirmed; major.minor only per the source (no patch byte reported)

pollingRate._needsVerification: raw<->Hz table not transcribed -- this reads the raw register value only. Pulsar's Nordic mice are typically 125/250/500/1000/2000/4000/8000 Hz; do not assume the raw byte is one of these until confirmed with `hskctl get pollingRate` next to the Pulsar Fusion app.

dpiStageCount._needsVerification: address and width transcribed, not confirmed

activeDpiStage._needsVerification: source describes this as 0-based, unlike the G-Wolves profile's 1-based activeDpiStage -- do not compare the two raw

liftOffDistance._needsVerification: map transcribed from source, not confirmed on hardware

debounceMs._needsVerification: described as milliseconds directly (0-30), unlike the G-Wolves profile's opaque table-row byte -- still unconfirmed

sleepSeconds._needsVerification: 'units of 10s' per the source; scale applied here so the field speaks seconds like the G-Wolves profile does

_followUp: VID/PID and reportId (6) are confirmed on real hardware for the cabled connection; the RF receiver's own config-endpoint interface is still not identified -- a fresh `hskctl probe --json` with the dongle connected, now that all five product ids are in match.productIds, may score it differently.

The opcode/address byte layout is still the pre-existing transcription, unconfirmed and evidently at least partly wrong (real hardware returns no data at all cabled, and duplicate garbage values for different fields over the dongle). Static analysis of the real app (tools/analyze-driver.py) confirmed the transport (HID Feature reports, real HidD_SetFeature/HidP_GetCaps imports) but not the packet bytes -- native C++/MFC embeds those as immediate values in machine code, not as an extractable blob the way G-Wolves' .NET FieldRVA tables were. Getting them needs either real disassembly of 'Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe', or a live USB capture (Wireshark/usbmon) while it runs against a real X2H mini.
Confirm every _needsVerification field with `hskctl get <field>` next to the Pulsar Fusion app once real packet bytes are known, then delete the marker so writes unlock.

DPI stage values and LED colour need a record-level checksum (0x55 - value per byte, not the whole-packet checksum) that protocol.py does not support yet -- add an encoding for it before mapping dpiStage1..N here. Cfg.ini confirms this model ships 4 DPI stages by default (400/800/1600/3200), not 7 like the G-Wolves profile.
